corrections.claim: INVENTORY.md:278 gives the Storage_Sufficient slot term as Θ(N·S⁴).
corrections.correction: The successful invariant checks each earlier slot again, in addition to the body and Post. The slot term is Θ(N²·S⁴) for uniform independently varying slot length S. This does not change the dominant Θ(N⁶) Python-sized, bounded-value family.

corrections.claim: H4 / INVENTORY.md:693 and inventory.json hazards group direct Contained/Sum as Θ(N³·L⁵).
corrections.correction: Sum alone performs quadratic, not cubic, worst-case Value work through its processed-prefix invariant. Cubic Value work belongs to Contained with repeated parent identities. The Check-path distinction based on Shape uniqueness is sound. Sum_Reference also scans excluded rows and identity bytes, so its cost cannot depend only on the number of included rows.

corrections.claim: H7 / INVENTORY.md:617,696 summarize owner/retry exports as fixed Θ(L⁶); Appendix A:916 labels Retry_Equation O(H·id).
corrections.correction: Individual epoch comparisons have fixed multiplicity, but retry authorization and audit traverse whole histories. Retry_Holds, Retry_Reference and Retry_Equation call History_Valid, and audit Same_Prefix calls Same_Row with Same_Epoch per row. The whole exported paths require history-dependent terms and a full trace; they are not fixed Θ(L⁶) or O(H·id).

corrections.claim: H6 / INVENTORY.md:595 states Θ(D²·L⁵ + D·L⁶) without a nonempty-disk qualification.
corrections.correction: Empty disk rosters still execute Check_Capacity and its checked numeric relation. Include that fixed memory-quantity cost or state explicitly that the displayed class is a nonempty, comparable-extent worst-case envelope. Similar composite Θ expressions are not equalities for every short-circuit path.

corrections.claim: INVENTORY.md:114 says every Big_Integer operation allocates its result; :125-129 describes each PR invocation as exactly one multiply/result allocation/Post literal/variant.
corrections.correction: Comparisons return Boolean without allocating a Big_Integer result. PR invocations remain a valid source call-count unit, but the exponent-zero body has no multiply, nonzero bodies also convert 256, and predicates/controlled copies add work. Do not report the invocation count as an exact allocation or machine instruction count. The stated polynomial limb-work classes remain conditional source-model reasoning.

corrections.claim: INVENTORY.md:372-373,673-674 cites chain C API call/handler at lines 114/117 and run-ledger handler at 221.
corrections.correction: In the hash-matched candidate, the chain W.Decide call is line 99 and exception handler line 102. The run-ledger handler is line 222; line 221 is the normal return 0. The failure-mapping conclusion survives, but these evidence locations must be repaired.

corrections.claim: INVENTORY.md:785-788,800-803 gives gap-multiplied cost classes without an ordered nonzero-gap qualification.
corrections.correction: Allowed zero-gap calls still evaluate Posts over absolute positions. Packet 13 Prefix_Tail gains an absolute Prefix_Reference Post even when First=Stop; Prefix_Decomposition also has absolute reference work at its base. Packet 12's unchanged Posts retain radix/prefix cost at Low=High. Use nonzero-gap qualifications or retain these base terms; do not discard equal-endpoint cases.

corrections.claim: INVENTORY.md:807 / inventory.json packet 12 says the changed witnesses are reached only on mismatch lemmas, once per call.
corrections.correction: One outer mismatch can trigger many nested witness evaluations. The unchanged Worldline.Resources Prefix_Modulus calls Prefix_Quotient at every recursive level; a Mismatching_Sum_Column invokes Value_Modulus for multiple operands. Looping the inner witness removes its own recursion, not the containing recursion or repeated calls. The advertised standalone polynomial classes remain conditional worst-case classes before and after.

corrections.claim: INVENTORY.md:818-822 says base-to-candidate diffs consist of parenthesization, nonrecursive contradiction lemmas, and a canonical invariant/case subtype.
corrections.correction: The textual delta description is incomplete. It also changes default initializations and predicated Ghost local types, adds column/prefix assertions, introduces a Canonicalize Ghost slot constant, and adds an array-length guard in Tagged_Matches while removing the Invalid_Value case. These inspected changes do not alter the dominant cost classes identified here, but the narrower textual description is false; semantic equivalence and source qualification remain separate obligations.

corrections.claim: INVENTORY.md:708-710 labels whole-file-pinned body changes L plus reviewed pin regeneration, while :714-715 reserves O for public spec/reference/contract/API/ABI/runtime/build changes.
corrections.correction: Keep implementation ownership distinct from permission to change pinned text. Under this review's requested pinned-text boundary, a concrete change to enrolled pinned text must carry O-PINS operator approval as well as independent review and regenerated effective pins. Body-only implementation work can be lead-owned; that label does not authorize changing the protected pin package, weakening its keyset, or adopting a changed pinned contract/reference. This review authorizes none of those actions.
evidence: user review item 4: operator approval for pinned text or public contract

corrections.claim: INVENTORY.md:752 labels narrower Ghost copies L and says constant-factor only.
corrections.correction: Narrowing an arena snapshot to a changing slot can change the copy component's growth when arena and slot extents vary independently, although a dominant arithmetic class may remain. It also needs a reviewed way to preserve the original whole-arena frame relations. If existing assertions/relations are replaced, R is required; pinned-text or public-contract changes retain their O boundary. Native allocation/copy-lifetime improvement is not established statically.

corrections.claim: INVENTORY.md:755-756 labels failure-code differentiation L+R, ABI review, possibly O.
corrections.correction: Internal diagnostics that preserve the public interface can be L+R. A changed public transport code, meaning, layout, or caller protocol is an API/ABI package and requires O, not discretionary 'possibly O'. All original accepted cases and native success obligations remain fixed; a clearer failure classification supplies no native acceptance.

hazard_rulings.ruling: Correct source-semantic exponential duplication: one recursive body call and one recursive Post call; Replay_Reference repeats in its own Post, and Wire.Decide invokes it in each result-field conjunct. Valid-genesis retained-row mismatch paths also pay full reference recursion. No measured native cost is established.

hazard_rulings.ruling: Whole-output and total-arena evaluation is real; Python-sized bounded-value growth remains the quoted high-order family. Correct the independent slot term (C-SLOT); generic Ada arena/slot parameters and empty cases need explicit bounds.
hazard_rulings.evidence_class: observed source plus conditional static growth reasoning

hazard_rulings.ruling: Correct reference hierarchy: nonrecursive primitive Posts, linear self-recursion in public Posts, iterative worker invariant reconstruction, repeated Magnitude/Value evaluation. PR calls are a proxy rather than exact allocations or elapsed work; runtime threshold is assessed in item 2.
hazard_rulings.evidence_class: observed source plus static recurrence reasoning; exact JACKAL arithmetic

hazard_rulings.ruling: Check-path uniqueness distinction is supported. Correct direct Sum versus Contained and excluded-row scan cost (C-SUM). Wire decoding repeats checked Decode/equality work.
hazard_rulings.evidence_class: observed source plus conditional static reasoning

hazard_rulings.ruling: Can_Reserve success-path column and Post structure and Try_Reserve Matching_Prefix amplification are supported. Sum_Equals's displayed class is for the success path; its mismatch invokes recursive modulus/quotient witnesses and is not covered by that headline.

hazard_rulings.ruling: Prior-disk invariant/reference reevaluation is supported; add empty-roster memory work (C-EMPTY).
hazard_rulings.evidence_class: observed source plus conditional static reasoning

hazard_rulings.ruling: Pending, completion and history structures are supported. Owner/retry full exported-path claims need correction and retracing (C-OWNER); explicitly untraced completion/finalization exports remain unverified.

hazard_rulings.ruling: The listed quantifiers rescan processed prefixes and nested references under Check. Treat classes as source-level worst-case component envelopes; early existential/universal termination and byte-comparison extents matter. Initialized itself is not a runtime proof of validity; Decode/equality quantifiers supply the listed work.

hazard_rulings.ruling: Ghost snapshots, Old captures and linear recursion depth are present. Native primary/secondary stack layout, peak live heap, copy elision and exhaustion behavior are not determined statically.

open_obligations.target: Production refuses every reproduced promotion defect: A (failed-check return), B (leftover synthetic world), C (undeclared empty roster), D (failed agent) and the typed-absence scenarios.

Each world has exactly one effective evaluation: the newest completed evaluation under the current requirement, PASS or FAIL, selected by the proved kernel. A newer evaluation supersedes every older one, and a superseded evaluation never regains authority (roadmap Phase 1 item 5).

A candidate can never change the requirement that judges it or any later candidate: policy, verifier scope, protected set and examiners. The proved kernel refuses any such change (including a rewritten authoritative verifier, VERIFIER_MODIFIED_BY_CANDIDATE) in every promotion mode.

A verdict that can authorize promotion comes from an examiner candidate code cannot reach or steer: determinate supervision (SUPERVISED, not stopped) and no candidate code in the examiner's process or identity (os._exit(0), unittest.SkipTest, monkeypatching can never yield an admitted PASS).

Every check that can authorize promotion binds a verifier identity staged from PRIME covering everything it executes or imports, including the process that actually decides the verdict (argv program and interpreter script operand), or the policy is refused at load.
The promoted bytes are exactly the bytes examined before any check ran, immutable for the whole evaluation. Nothing a check, or candidate code it ran, wrote during checking can become PRIME.

A report verdict is PASS only if at least one testcase executed and none failed, errored or was skipped, and a benchmark regression is FAIL. The verdict is computed in SPARK from facts produced independently of Python (Report_Facts).

No code from the candidate tree ever executes inside the examiner principal, and a PASS counts only when every import and read resolved inside the staged verifier bundle or the standard library; otherwise the check is EVALUATOR_INCOMPLETE. The evidence identifies every trusted input that influenced the verdict.
An admitted report's verdict cannot be supplied by the candidate; a report that carries bytes the candidate wrote is not admissible.
Candidate bytes never run under the worker principal; every candidate process runs as the candidate principal.
Examiner, worker and candidate have nested user-namespace creation disabled, as worlds and checks do (--disable-userns), and a private role provably cannot leave its cgroup budget.
A case copy or frozen copy equals one consistent state of its source, even under a deliberate racing writer.
Report boundary facts (mount exclusivity, role identity) are observed independently of the bootstrap before a report is admitted.
Each required verdict depends only on the pre-check snapshot and its PRIME examiner.
Only the policy authority changes live PRIME; no candidate code can.
The candidate has no veto over supersession (M3 soundness-1).

The v2 claim: a candidate cannot plant a judge that takes over at the next primary switch. Neither a non-primary .worldline.json nor any examiner it names can be changed by a candidate and later adopted.
The v1 claim: the requirement covers every file in a verifier scope, so any candidate change an examiner could observe there is REQUIREMENT_CHANGED.
Staged bytes that differ from the candidate are refused; they are never published as a PRIME checkpoint that can later be returned to.
An agent whose subprocess was OOM-killed, or that hit a resource ceiling, is never PASS.
In production every examiner that a registered root's policy names is protected against candidate writes.

A FAIL under a requirement is terminal for that (world, requirement), and requesting an evaluation is a controlled capability, so re-running a flaky or host-dependent check cannot produce an authorizing PASS.

Collapse, return, transaction commit, abort, prune, revalidation requests, simulate and ghost enable are per-requester capabilities decided daemon-side (and for promotion, by the kernel). A commit's follow-on effects (starting PRIME's declared services, opening terminals and moving windows on the daemon account's desktop after a return) belong to the requester's capability, not free side effects, and a delegated socket fd confers nothing beyond its grant. Every receipt and causal event records the requester, hashed into the chain.
No listed-client act changes the judge in force; restoring an older policy needs an owner capability that binds the requirement it adopts.
A superseded evaluation never regains authority, including across an engine rollback.
A checkpoint return restores exactly the bytes checkpoint S had when displaced (S.components and content_id), witnessed by S's own committed receipt, and the kernel decides this.
Re-application re-applies only W's evaluated bytes: W's delta_hash and components are verified against the re-applied payload and manifests.

The promotion mode is derived from authenticated facts (the prepared transaction's typed mode), whether a return subject was ever live PRIME is decided by the proved Worldline.Ancestry over chained lineage records, and no alias can collide with an instance_id or content_id.
Commit authorizes only if PRIME, the candidate payload and the record schema are what prepare saw, decided in the kernel.

Every identity pair Decide compares is produced from two independent records, and a value copied to both sides (or a wrong digest stated on both) cannot reach AUTHORIZED; Resulting_Requirement is never computed from live PRIME.

Promotion admissibility is decided in SPARK from raw observations: every decode/validate step on the authorization path is proved (as Collapse_Wire.Decode is), and Decide recomputes roster completeness itself.
The status that speaks at promotion is re-derived from the retained report bytes by proved or independently produced code, so a store rewrite of the status is refused.
It is proved that an evaluation that did not complete never satisfies Roster_Complete.
A revalidation context states exactly the requirement and verifier bytes its checks ran under, from one generation-guarded read, and stored base manifests are verified with verify_content.

Evidence is a statement about particular bytes under particular rules, including the interpreter, argv0 binaries and their libraries, sandbox and toolchain binaries and the forwarded environment; any change to them makes evidence stale.
Commit recomputes Resulting_Requirement from a location derived from the transaction id, never from JSON.

Every change to live PRIME that no record accounts for is measured, ownership included, and content identity covers ownership; a receipt never states foreignWorldContamination NONE while an unmeasured change is present.

Two trees with the same content root behave the same, and payload integrity covers every field that can change behaviour; any exclusion is proven behaviour-neutral and stated in the kernel-facing spec.
Every Decide is answered by the exact proved kernel build named in a root-owned, signed proof manifest; a substituted library can neither authorize a promotion nor obtain a PROVED receipt.

Commit and recovery decide only on facts they recompute or on prepare-time facts, evaluation records, contexts, executed-verifier sets, history entries and epochs authenticated with a key a same-uid process cannot use; consistent forgery is detected and refused.

The values that reach the kernel are computed by proved code, or by an independent producer, from raw records: canonical encoding is injective and manifests, content roots and requirement identities are complete.
The bytes exchanged into PRIME are exactly the bytes the kernel authorized and the receipt's afterRoot and PRIME row name.
Whitepaper principle 1: nothing becomes real except through an authorized collapse; every PRIME generation change is a kernel-checked transition.
Every primary succession is explicit and receipted: root.remove of the primary refuses unless the successor is named, and the switch records the requirement it adopts.

Every change to the requirement in force produces one ordered, receipted judge-change record (requirement before and after) through a mechanised owner-authorized path: live PRIME write, reconcile, restart resetting dirty, root.add/root.remove, engine or configuration change, checkpoint return.

Production promotions pass through the composed Authority v1 transaction (intent gate, capability issuer with consumed use, live examiner evidence chain, resource ledger, Universe registry), and the capability, evidence and Universe protected heads are composed and owned by the production authority. Mediation is enforced by the OS, not by convention: the daemon account's Python cannot mutate live PRIME except through the protected actuator, every actuation is re-observed and bound to durable transaction evidence, and a bypass campaign on the production topology shows it (roadmap Phase 2 exit gate).
Supervision facts (SUPERVISED, STOPPED, exit) come from an authenticated manager source that a same-uid process cannot forge and that does not depend on journal persistence.
The unproved C surface is minimal (null check, call, exception-to-255 mapping) and every data-handling path, including hashing marshalling, is proved.

Every PRIME publication, including one completed by crash recovery, is authorized by a kernel decision recovery re-derives; recovery marks COMMITTED only after verifying that live/<key> resolves to the authorized staged payload and a durable one-shot authorization exists, otherwise it aborts or quarantines; an offline write is never folded into a collapse generation.
A missing or altered config never lowers protection: network, resource ceilings and anchor export default closed; the config is integrity-bound; operator edits are never overwritten.

Admission is decided by a proved rule and fails closed: it refuses when its ledger is missing, observes under its lock, meters all work including checks, doctor --refresh and git inspection, and its reservations satisfy the proved invariants of OB-198 (conservation, parent/child containment, no double release, no running workload without an active reservation), with the resource epoch an input to Decide (roadmap-requirements.md:105, :108).
The daemon refuses to serve clients when its unit, drop-ins, install tree or account are writable by a client.
No account is in both the client group and the daemon's group.
The data-directory gate is open only while a daemon that checked the content is running; any ambiguity (hard-linked lock, cannot tell, relative XDG path) closes it.
At most one daemon ever serves a store, and store ownership, type and schema are checked before any write.
Every binary the private boundary relies on is digest-pinned in the run plan and re-checked before use.
The host identities mapped to worker and candidate belong to no other account on the host.
The isolation boundary (what a world, check, examiner or worker can see and write) is checked against a declared specification on every build.
Every digest equality Decide proves rests on a hash implementation proved to compute SHA-256 (functional postconditions, not only absence of runtime errors).
The broker commits only promotions admitted by the intent gate and bound to the gate-journaled operation and capability, whatever the caller's uid.
No promotion commits under a revoked grant; the broker rechecks the capability under its own lock before commit, and a queued recover cannot resume a promote the operator stopped.
Capability ID uniqueness is enforced against the custody registry, with the C ABI, adapter and replay inside the proof boundary.
Every daemon fact the root broker relies on is authenticated or independently re-derived, and evidence covers each fact.
The evidence binding pins the gate config and the Universe Genesis, so evidence cannot be replayed under another gate or Universe.
Nowhere in the authority stack does missing equal missing, or read as zero, empty or pass.
Protected child admission is fully authorized (Create_Child authority).
The Genesis roster is bound to its policy.
Quiet(U) is fed the observed counts of running worlds, reservations and unresolved transactions as Optional values, and Can_Advance_Prime requires Generation = Prime_Generation + 1.
Hierarchy conservation is proved in SPARK.
Issuer reconciliation verifies the event chain from the anchored head before accepting any state.
The daemon singleton lease holds against a hostile same-UID process.

No agent and no process of the operator account can obtain root or write production state outside the protected path: sudo requires a password no agent has seen, docker (root-equivalent) membership is gone from every running process, the only NOPASSWD rule left is a reviewed read-only helper, and a bypass campaign run from the operator account itself (no sudo, no docker) against the installed production boundary shows it (operator directive section 1).
No version can be installed without an accepted assurance of the exact tagged commit, whatever the repository settings or workflow edits.
Abort never deletes a payload live PRIME resolves to and never acts on a quarantined transaction.
Prune deletes only the requester's own history, never another client's worlds or lineage return targets without an owner capability, and walks paths race-free.
An exchange that happened is always recorded COMMITTED, durably and with its receipt, across any crash, and PRIME is never a torn tree.
No unrecorded PRIME write is frozen into a fork under a stale parent: dirty state survives restart and freeze measures live against the PRIME row.

No write into live PRIME that WORLDLINE did not make is lost or published under a collapse receipt: every such write is refused before the exchange or recorded as an unaccounted-write with its bytes preserved.
root remove either carries every write to the operator's path or refuses.

Every write into live PRIME not made by WORLDLINE is observed and accounted (as a generation or a foreign write) even if reverted, including mmap writes and writes through external hard links, and freeze and reconcile consult coverage.
Relocation proves every retained payload and generation in the copy equals its recorded content identity.
A payload absence is exempted only on evidence the tool can verify.
A rolled-back local ledger is detected against a history-keeping external witness before any export, and export failures are reported.

PROVED in a receipt means the running library is the product of a zero-exception proof, at or above the floor with pinned contracts, run for this library, and a skipped proof or malformed manifest never yields PROVED.

The proof gate pins every contract authority depends on (receipts, causal_graph, world, ancestry as well as collapse, wire, identities, evaluation, transitions) and parses GNATprove output fail-closed with summarySha256 checked.
Receipts, the causal chain and stored validation contexts are tamper-evident against any process except the daemon's own authority.
An anchor copy the attacker cannot write always exists, so a store rewrite is always detectable.
Causal events are appended to the signed, exported anchor too.
The anchor signs only receipts it has verified, checks coverage by receipt identity, and pins its public key.

The receipt chain binds transaction ids and has an externally witnessed genesis and head, so tail deletion and re-pointing are detected, and receipts are issued only from authenticated records. Chain acceptance and verification go through the exported, proved Worldline.Receipts.Append and Causal_Graph.Append (OB-197), never a Python comparison (roadmap Phase 1 item 6).
Only WORLDLINE can author events with reserved actors or kinds, and why separates agent claims from WORLDLINE facts.
The CLI verifies that the server peer is the daemon account before trusting any answer.
Any signalled process in the inspection sandbox refuses the inspection.
A receipt independently evidences the judge in force after it, so a later reader can check which requirement a return restored.
The full transaction lifecycle relation and the world-state relation are proved contracts.
An install, upgrade or documented rollback never kills the shell while a plugin rescan is running, including the rescan the watcher starts when the checkout moves.
When install.sh exits 0 the shell runs the installed commit's keepLoaded service and overlay.

The plugin never shows a world as PASS or eligible when its newest evaluation is FAIL or ERROR, and renders REQUIREMENT_CHANGED, EVIDENCE_SUPERSEDED, UNBOUND, TIMED_OUT, ERROR outcome, source revalidation-incomplete and the doctor 'failed' class.
The production anchor keeps its independent ATTEST cross-check and a history-keeping external witness.
Agent worlds are network-contained by default, with egress limited to the adapter's provider hosts plus a declared allow list; 'shared' is an explicit, recorded opt-in.
Every sandbox that runs candidate or client-supplied code, including system futures (simulate), follows the configured network policy, so an audition has no real network side effects.
An agent never holds a long-lived real credential it could exfiltrate.
Allowed egress is limited to the provider API's intended use and cannot carry arbitrary exfiltration.
No client-supplied code ever runs as the daemon account, with or without network (SECURITY.md:472-475, :563-564).
A client never obtains through the daemon content its own file access would forbid.
Clients can reach only current PRIME content.
WORLDLINE itself enforces exact memory, swap and task bounds on repository inspection whatever the unit says, and under memory pressure the kernel always kills inspection, never the daemon.
install.sh and rollback.sh never leave the session less secured than they found it.
No test or review scenario can reach the live desktop's tools or sessions by any route (PATH, absolute path, session socket); the original header said host tools 'can never be touched'.
No role receives an identifier from outside the sandbox.
Root-private authority state is confidential against loss of the backup device.
The harness proves 'restart or rescan, never both' for every way the installer can reach the shell, whenever it happens, so a regression cannot pass CI.
The harness's discriminating power is itself gated: every modelled defect is checked into the repository and must fail the harness on every CI run.

Every shipped script that can reload the shell (engine install.sh, scripts/rollback.sh, plugin install.sh) is mechanically gated against rescan-then-restart in CI, running the release artifact's post-build path.
A full assurance run of the exact tagged commit: every test runs on at least one required runner, and a missing, failing or skipped step fails the run (SECURITY.md:202-213).
Release provenance beyond the GitHub account: signed tags and assets verified before install (implied by the manifest's 'signing' field and --signing option).
The relocation holder match is exact on btrfs and exercised on a real btrfs filesystem in required assurance.
The evaluation oracle is exhaustive for both Classify and Admissible.
It is checked systematically that 1.10.0 authorizes nothing production 1.7.3 refuses, outside declared classes.
While any transaction is quarantined (RECOVERY_INCOMPLETE) every store-mutating operation is refused until recovery settles it.
Every deferred review finding is listed with its closure obligation or its fix and test.
Operation, transaction, Universe, capability and evidence IDs are distinct types that cannot be confused in any comparison.
Every failed durable write in the broker path stops the service, so memory never leads disk.
The handoff protection is evidenced against the class of socket swap and handoff attacks.
Every part of audit finding 9 is closed (DIRECTIVE:71-75).
The approval binds the complete rehearsal record, including failed runs.
Before the install, production state is checked against 1.9.x assumptions.
A committed collapse or return is always reported as committed; post-commit failures are warnings, never the result, and every committed generation eventually gets its automatic ghosts.
The original claim: 'inotify unavailable' is answered with the typed refusal MEASUREMENT_ABSENT (PRIME_WATCH_UNAVAILABLE for fork) while the daemon keeps serving non-mutating operations.
PRIME stability across the whole authorization, up to the exchange, is decided by the proved kernel (the 1.9.0 headline: 'PRIME stability and watch coverage are measured and decided in the kernel').
One authority: every promotion precondition is a kernel refusal with its own code.
Report integrity VERIFIED is a kernel decision over typed facts.
Classify has a full functional specification: every observation region maps to exactly one specified classification.
No process with an identity more privileged than the candidate's is visible inside the candidate's PID namespace.
Finalization, doctor and validation report a world whose staged merge would change the requirement as 'can never promote', so fresh predicts REQUIREMENT_CHANGED.
Every production fact the migration depends on is verified read-only against production before install.
Every root that can become primary has a policy whose required checks are bound and whose verdicts candidate code cannot choose.
aegis-anubis's bound check judges the candidate's .anb files.

Admissible, candidate-isolated report checks for the project's real workflows (pytest, make test, prove.sh/GNATprove), a proof-workflow binding of a deployed library, and a tree contract covering symlinks and xattrs.

Neither the candidate nor a transient infrastructure fault controls promotion: candidate-induced failures supersede, infrastructure faults are attributed and retried without an operator-run revalidate.
Every revalidation request for a known world leaves a speaking record, so a payload corruption becomes a speaking ERROR head.
Every check's captured output is bounded in bytes and time.
Prepare and finalization finish in bounded time whatever a candidate places in a verifier scope.
Plain argument tokens are treated as arguments, and any failure to identify a verifier gives a named refused record, not a DEAD world.
The runtime moves every check through the kernel's Transition_Allowed/Advance and persists each step, so recovery knows where an evaluation stopped.
The daemon always starts, quarantines any unrecoverable transaction durably, and a quarantine is cleared by a recorded owner action, never by hand edits.
Roots can be registered in a dedicated deployment through an authorized flow.
The daemon unit and user manager run with RestrictSUIDSGID=yes, the hardening 1.7.0 recommended, with every sandbox working.
Client mode refuses to start unless the host mounts the store nosuid.
A client cannot make PRIME uncapturable.
Collapse prepare works for any tree that can be captured, including non-empty 0555 directories, with final modes preserved.
A declined return leaves nothing behind and can be retried at the same PRIME; no later collapse is blocked by its leftovers.
Return vehicles and PRIME generations live in disjoint identity spaces, so a declined return can never block or corrupt a later collapse.
Any tree WORLDLINE can capture can be materialized by fork, prepare and revalidation.
Every path that starts work, including disk for the revalidation copy, asks the admission authority first and refuses before consuming space it was not granted.
Watch coverage of PRIME is continuous across a watcher rebuild, so no event is lost.
Re-applying a candidate follows the collapse rules and succeeds when fresh evidence exists.
A long or refused revalidation never blocks other daemon requests.
A registration is atomic: it commits only content checked after the move.
Publication is atomic: either the world is recorded and PRIME moved, or neither.
The check that no daemon holds the lock and the close of the gate are one atomic step.
Repository content cannot forge git's failure reports, and doctor's rootIntegrity matches what captures do.
No filesystem stall can block the daemon from answering requests.
Before serving, the daemon refuses by name any deployment it cannot operate in.
doctor reports every deployment requirement WORLDLINE depends on, and the tools it actually executes.
Only the inspected root and the minimal files git needs are visible to repository-controlled code.
The daemon reclaims everything its evaluations created, including copies owned by subordinate IDs.

No retained payload is ever lost by the store; a payload that disappears anyway (outside the store's control) is detected at start, doctor and relocation, and the world is recorded INCOMPLETE with a causal event.
Relocation reads the old store's full committed state, or refuses by name when it cannot.
Relocation refuses while any process holds the copy's database open.
Relocation positively proves the copy is not the old store in every case, and distinguishes a legitimate bind-mounted copy (for example ostree /var) from a view of the old store.
Relocation verifies or neutralizes everything in the copy.
After install or rollback the desktop runs exactly one plugin commit.
The ABI layout the runtime writes is by construction the layout SPARK decodes.
The vendored proved SHA-256 units are bound to a recorded upstream commit and file digests that the proof gate verifies (the purpose of core/attest/sync.sh).

Admitted work holds real, enforced reservations so it can finish, and the reservation rules are proved (OB-198: conservation, containment, no double release, no running workload without an active reservation) with a resource epoch in Decide.
Evidence states which model produced a world, with provider attestation where available, and says UNATTESTED otherwise.
For every consequential action it starts, the plugin shows the engine's actual outcome.
The evaluator's readiness is decided by liveness, not a fixed wall-clock guess.
Assurance is deterministic on slower runners.
Evidence rows are per operation, and an abort at EVIDENCE_REQUIRED is recoverable without operator surgery.
Every release path is exercised on the installed service; PREPARED-abort-then-release releases only after proving no commit happened, and survives the endpoint reseal.
Every broker phase has a proven recovery or abandon path.
A crash between the protected service's C answer and the saved ACTUATOR_BROKER_COMMITTED event is reconciled automatically.
A durable refusal is followed by automatic reconciliation that resumes authorized progress.
One requester cannot deny service to another, and every create resolves to a definite state.
Legacy capability rows are migrated or quarantined by a trusted, recorded decision.
Work, the root-private /srv labs and the live WORLDLINE state are fully backed up and restore-verified.
The operator can inspect repository-root history safely without trusting config the account wrote.
Installer rollback copies stay available with the production store.
The dead-man reverts only after its intended confirmation window.
The distributed plugin is the fixed 1.3.4.

The plugin says 'not committed' or 'no file changed' only when the engine reports the transaction ABORTED or DENIED. It reads the engine's reported state (details.state): a committed state with a post-commit error shows COMMITTED with the warning, and an unknown code or a deadline shows 'outcome unknown, check status'.
The plugin names, explains and classifies (refused, committed with a warning, unknown) every code its paired engine can return, including 1.9.0's kernel codes 15-20 and the runtime codes 1.9.0 added.

Each engine release binds the plugin it is compatible with (tag, commit, archive digest, supported code-set digest) into its release manifest, and install.sh installs only a plugin commit the manifest names, so every artifact is bound to one accepted state (roadmap-requirements.md:427).

A verification command exits nonzero whenever anything it verifies is not intact: a BROKEN, MISMATCH, ROLLED_BACK or EXPORT_BEHIND anchor, a broken causal or receipt chain, or a canonical file outside the store's events/ and receipts/ directories. Every refusal path has a test.

A receipt or causal event is appended only when the proved Worldline.Receipts.Append or Causal_Graph.Append accepts it (the supplied predecessor equals the chain head), and verification replays the chain through the same proved rule (roadmap-requirements.md:110: 'Formalize capability attenuation and receipt-chain rules').

Reservation conservation, parent/child allocation containment, no double release and no running workload without an active reservation are proved in SPARK, and the collapse rule takes a resource epoch as a typed input (roadmap-requirements.md:105, :108).

Only the listed client uids and the daemon account can read PRIME's content or the published status; client mode refuses to start when the client group has any member, named or by primary gid, outside the uid list.

Post-commit effects run only under the requester's capability: a client that may not run the owner-only `switch` cannot make the daemon account start services, open terminals or move windows, and a process holding a delegated socket fd gets no authority beyond the grant bound to it.

Installing or upgrading WORLDLINE never destroys operator configuration: a symlinked shell.json or bindings.lua is edited through its target with its mode kept, an operator binding is displaced only with the operator's recorded consent and restored on rollback, and operator edits inside the managed block are preserved or the install refuses with a diff.
The daemon always starts and runs recovery: a failure to stop an orphaned unit is recorded on the job, never an exception that aborts the start before recover_all.

Registering roots publishes a PRIME generation that is a stable snapshot of exactly the registered content, decided like every other PRIME mutation (one transition service); a write during registration is refused or recorded, never folded in.

The production boundary holds against the operator account itself: from `sicarii`, with no sudo and no docker, every direct write to /srv/worldline and live PRIME, every socket request beyond the client operations and every unit or config edit is refused, shown by a retained campaign against the installed production boundary (operator directive section 1).

The anchor key can be rotated: a rotation is an anchored, verifiable entry signed by the old key (or an owner-recorded retirement when the old key is compromised), the ledger verifies across rotations, and the current key's fingerprint is pinned outside the daemon account's write access.
After the move only the signer (the worldline account now; a separate signer later, OB-086) can sign production anchor entries.
No retained payload is lost by WORLDLINE, and when one is found missing its cause is established and prevented.
A backup refuses, or reports INCOMPLETE by name, when any configured or discovered source cannot be read; success means every source was captured.

A verified rollback exists for production as it is now (DIRECTIVE:10-13, 'Keep a verified rollback'): drilled after a reboot and after the sudo cutover, at production scale, with kills in the middle of a step's change, for the exact release to be installed.

Production evaluates candidates with the checks their policies declare (GNAT, anb, mise tools) and runs the agents the operator approves, from root-owned toolchains and a credential custody the daemon account can use without reading the operator's home.

Resource reservation, consumption and release are decided by a proved rule over quantities bound to the actual host and workload accounting of the same protected Universe and broker transaction (AUTHORITY-OPERATIONS.md:15; roadmap-requirements.md:108).

Each permanent fault campaign (power loss, SIGKILL during evaluation and actuation, disk full, read-only filesystem, corrupt store, stale evidence, missing and changed verifier, same-uid attack, namespace edge cases, reused nonce, cross-run result substitution, clock jump, network loss, provider timeout, OOM, cgroup manager or systemd restart, daemon restart, partial installation, rollback, concurrent prepare, concurrent commit) has a retained reproducer, target identity, expected legal outcome and actual observations for the release under test (roadmap-requirements.md:394-419).
After the production move, no drill or rehearsal account, subordinate ID range, unit, timer, group membership or directory remains unless it is recorded as deliberately kept.

'Run the repaired adversarial campaign against the final PR source and retain valid attacker artifacts and complete results' (roadmap-requirements.md:61): every window the campaign names is reached with a retained attacker artifact and a recorded outcome.
Observing a receipt never executes configuration from the repository it names.
Question or mission text is always passed as an operand, never parsed as an option.
Item 4's full denial campaign: every direct and indirect path to an effect is denied on the installed lab, including /proc/<pid>/fd paths and an authentic Universe head change (DESIGN.md F8).
Every fault hook writes a signed marker proving it fired, and crash evidence captures the gate process's exit status with the registry and journal before recovery (DESIGN.md F1/F2).
A capability grant is consumed at most its ceiling of times, proved in SPARK, as part of capability attenuation (roadmap-requirements.md:110; DESIGN.md slice 1 item 7).
